g.text: Let's understand your project before generating the strategy.
What is the name of your project?
→ e.g., MyApp, E-commerce Platform, Banking API
Briefly describe what the product does. What problem does it solve and who are the users?
→ e.g., A mobile app for tracking personal finances, used by individual consumers
: B2C SaaS platform with user authentication, subscription billing, and a feature-rich dashboard
served to end consumers via browser.
What type of product are we testing?
, REST API, microservices, embedded system, desktop app
What is the main technology stack?
→ e.g., React + Node.js, Java Spring Boot, Python Django, Flutter, .NET
: React, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, AWS (EC2, S3, RDS)
How many people are on the QA team?
'no dedicated QA — developers test their own code'
How many developers are on the team?
What is the project timeline or release deadline?
Does the team follow Agile, Waterfall, or another methodology?
Are there any known high-risk areas or critical features?
→ e.g., payment processing, user authentication, data migration, third-party integrations, performance under
: Third-party payment and OAuth integrations, authentication/session security, GDPR data handling
Does the project have any existing automated tests?
→ e.g., no automation yet, unit tests only, Selenium E2E suite, Postman API tests
: Playwright E2E test suite, Jest unit and integration tests
Are there any compliance or regulatory requirements?
→ e.g., legacy constraints, third-party dependencies, team specifics
